title: Results Section Audit
subject: checking optimality, timing, and deployment claims against solver-log evidence
eyebrow: Synthetic Results excerpt · no venue specified
summary: The excerpt reports solver statuses, a relative MIP-gap tolerance, timeouts, feasible incumbents, and final gaps for 12 instances. It does not support the universal exact-optimality and 10 s claim or the conclusion that the method is ready for real-time deployment.
footer: Generated on 4 August 2026 by applying the repository-local ieee-acm-paper-writing skill. The supplied excerpt is synthetic. The HTML is a presentation of the canonical text audit and adds no scientific finding.

findings.title: Global-optimum and 10 s guarantee is contradicted
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s.
findings.evidence: The supplied logs report that 3 of 12 runs reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%. The 9 OPTIMAL statuses were obtained under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, which does not establish exact global optimality.
findings.consequence: The sentence makes a universal exact-optimality and timing claim that is directly inconsistent with the reported failures and exceeds the stated certificate boundary.
findings.correction: Replace the sentence with a bounded report: 9 of 12 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, while 3 reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%. Do not call these results exact global optima or claim completion within 10 s.

findings.title: Timing and solver configuration are insufficiently reported
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s. Across 12 instances, 9 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, while 3 reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%.
findings.evidence: The excerpt supplies a 60 s limit, a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, statuses, and final gaps, but no solver identity or version, hardware, thread setting, seeds, or per-run timing measurements. The supplied record therefore cannot verify the 10 s statement or support reproducibility of the timing result.
findings.consequence: Readers cannot reconstruct the solver experiment or distinguish an observed runtime distribution from a claimed fixed time bound.
findings.correction: Provide the solver identity and version, hardware, thread and seed settings, stopping configuration, and per-instance runtime measurements. Until then, retain only the reported status, time-limit, feasibility, and gap observations.

findings.title: Real-time deployment readiness is unsupported
findings.source: The method is therefore ready for real-time deployment.
findings.evidence: No deployment experiment, operational validation, or timing measurements outside the solver logs are supplied. The same excerpt reports three time-limited runs with nonzero final gaps.
findings.consequence: The conclusion overgeneralizes bounded solver-log observations into an operational readiness claim and ignores failed or unresolved runs in the evaluated set.
findings.correction: Remove the deployment-readiness sentence. If real-time deployment is to be claimed, supply a deployment evaluation with its timing budget, workload, hardware, operational conditions, and treatment of the three time-limited runs; otherwise limit the conclusion to the reported solver-log results.
